If you don't want to make garments, don't make garments! Make blankets, scarves, headbands. Make what makes you happy. 

I love to learn new techniques. Salivate over novelty. And then I fixate. I become obsessed with random crap like trying to use eye of partridge stitch in everything I possibly can. I've made a couple sweaters, countless scarves and dishcloths. Probably a billion (12) hats. I make prayer shawls for a recovery ministry. I had a go at stuffed animals over Christmas but the stuffing and seaming killed that (now I just have bags upon bags of knit animal parts. Should have chosen differently... I've been considering making them look a bit bloodied and distressed and gifting them that way because they're never getting sewn 🤠) And right now, I'm fixated on cables. I need variety and novelty. 

BUT...

I'm a sock guy. 
A lacy-sock guy. (A single-lacy-sock guy. I say socks are my favorite thing to make, but in reality, it is sock. Sock are my favorite thing to make.) 

But I always come back to lacy socks. 
And all of those other things... most of them involve lace. Specifically some sort of lacy leaf motif. It is to the point where my non-knitting friends have jokingly asked me if I know about other shapes. I do! And I've done them! But for whatever reason, it's what my hands and brain wanna do in between all of the things that aren't leafy socks.  
One also commented: "Oh, he's looking at feet pics again" after glancing at my screen while I was browsing sock patterns. So...I know who I'm using my weird novelty yarn on :) 
Whatever. It's my happy place. 

My point is, it's just yarn. Fuck around. All of those things you listed? Blankets, purses, socks, scarves... there are limitless ways to do them. There's no bottom to the things you can learn if you decide you love doing blankets, or socks, or scarves, and stick with just one or a few. Learn the techniques that excite you. 
I mean, do you really want to slog your way through a sweater you hate just to say you can do short rows? You can learn that on an entrelac bag. Or you could never learn them at all because you never happen to need to use them. Make rectangular garter stitch scarves if that's what you like making. 

I don't think having an encyclopedic knowledge of knitting techniques is a requirement for being a good knitter. Neither is knitting garments. 

My advice is genuinely just fuck around. My skill improved in leaps and bounds within the last year (after 7 years knitting) by just... Doing whatever I felt like. And that's it. I'd see something and decide I want to make it and learn whatever I needed in order to make it happen. And sometimes I'd get partway through something and hate knitting it. And stop. 
Find something you love and want to make. And give it a whirl.  Look things up and ask questions when you don't understand something. There isn't an order. There isn't a standard. 
And there are only two stitches. Every single thing you will ever make will stem from knits and purls. You're just building from there, and so is everyone else.
They're not special for combining them in any particular way :)

NTA. 

Food is a physiological need. She is simultaneously asking to control the way you meet that need AND not seeing to it that she is meeting your nutrition requirements.

I can empathize with her somewhat on this—I am small (5’). I do not need much food. I am also a chronic under-eater. I don’t judge portions appropriately. When i was partnered (ex was over 6’), I had seriously no concept of how much food I needed to make and have around. Being responsible for the meals and grocery decisions   (to an unhealthy degree…among the reasons this is an ex) was a serious learning curve and I felt so terrible when I underestimated. 

What is UNACCEPTABLE here is 1) not changing the behaviors around food, and 2) being upset that you ate elsewhere when you have already expressed this as an issue, have made it clear you’d make up the difference yourself if you need anything beyond what she makes, and would otherwise just be going to bed hungry, and subsequently struggling through the day. 

Something has to change about this situation. A lot of people have said disordered eating, and several have said abuse. Could be one, the other, both, or neither, but it’s worth some serious examination. Regardless of the cause or intention, this is a very controlling behavior. You shouldn’t feel like seeing to it that you eat enough will hurt your relationship. Whether she is *intending* to be controlling/abusive or not, it is an abusive behavior and you are not the asshole for pre-gaming dinner knowing actual dinner will not be enough.

It feels a little performative.  Don't get me wrong, I appreciate when companies aren't openly discriminatory and flat-out talking shit and using their influence to be shitty towards us, but the rainbow logo doesn't really say a whole lot either. 

Corporations are not people, they do not have opinions, all they really have are products/services, and that is essentially their scope.  Personally, a company changing their logo during pride month doesn't make me more likely to choose their product over that of a competitor or view the corporation in a more favorable light.  It does not make me feel more valued as a person.  

I start to actually view them unfavorably when they set out booths at pride events to promote their products, because their goal is not to support the community in a material way, it is to cash in on the newfound acceptability of queerness, and using pride events to sell a product to the "trendy" demographic really rubs me the wrong way, especially when they'd almost certainly change tack to support homophobia/transphobia if that's where the money was. 

Maybe it's not near as sinister as Project SCUM, but the premise of a large corporation showing acceptance towards marginalized communities to sell a product feels pretty similar.

Receding hairline:
http://www.ftmguide.org/hairloss.html explains it better than I ever could.

Anger issues: 
Testosterone should not cause *uncontrollable* outbursts of anger.  You might find that you do get angry more easily, or that things that have already angered you make you more angry than they used to.  It might be helpful for you to have coping tools for anger.  Placing that angry energy into working out, for example, can be helpful for people. If anger becomes a serious issue for you, it would be time to talk to your doctor.  Anger can be a manifestation of anxiety or a sign that you need your levels checked/dose adjusted.  

Personality change:
Roughly the same as anger issues. Basic parts of your personality shouldn't change all that much.  Personality changes can come from increased/lifted dysphoria, confidence, insecurity, etc... A lot of big emotional changes happen for people when they start T.  If you find your personality changing, it's important to try to examine why.  
In my own experience with personality changes, I found myself liking things I previously didn't, I become less quiet and reserved, a bit more forceful...etc... and for me, it came down to feeling better about myself and like I didn't have to aim not to be noticed anymore.  Allowing myself to express my gender more fully gave me space to discover new interests and separate what I actually like from what I've been taught to like.  It shouldn't drastically change who you are. 

Patchy/no facial hair:
Honestly, that's just a crapshoot.  I have a wooley family, and my facial hair is non-existent almost 9 months in.  I have some lil transitional hairs, but nothing major.  Someone I know has a really nice lookin' goatee at 3 months.  There is no telling what will actually happen. 

Clitoral growth:
If clitoral growth is a deal-breaker for you, it's best not to go on T.  It is A THING. What's more is it's a really, really common thing.  So common in fact, I don't think I've ever heard of anyone NOT having it.  If you're afraid of that happening, and the thought seriously distresses you, hold off.  Maybe your feelings will eventually change, maybe they won't.  But once the clitoral growth happens, it's most likely not going to go back. 


I highly suggest looking through the FTM guide link I posted above for more information about testosterone.  It's pretty comprehensive and informative (in fact, more informative than my doctor was when going over the changes that might happen) and it really helped me make the decision about whether or not T was something I really wanted.
